1. Executive Summary & Lab Specifications Matrix

This report documents the implementation and comprehensive demonstration of an automated Assignment Submission Portal developed for the DevOps for Cloud Computing (CSC418) Lab Mid examination. The department's objective is to prevent regressions by automating quality assurance on every pushed revision, transmitting real-time execution telemetry to the instructor's local workstation, and enforcing quality-gated production releases.

Core Architecture & Highlights
All 5 Core Tasks (40 Marks) and both Bonus Tasks (10 Marks) have been completed, verified on automated CI runners, and deployed live. The system integrates Express.js, Jest, Supertest, GitHub Actions, Localtunnel/reverse relay, and Nodemailer SMTP delivery.

2. Task 1: Assignment Submission Portal (8 Marks)

The assignment submission portal allows students to submit required project links while strictly enforcing input validation rules before persisting records into memory or client storage.

2.1 Key Implementation Details

  • Mandatory Input Validation (src/validator.js): Enforces presence of name, regNo, and assignmentTitle as non-empty strings.
  • URL Integrity Sensor: Rejects invalid protocols (e.g., ftp://, local paths, or unparseable strings); strictly permits http:// and https://.
  • RESTful API (src/app.js): Exposes POST /api/submissions (returning HTTP 201 on success or HTTP 400 with descriptive error messages) and GET /api/submissions for listing submissions.
  • Dual-Mode Persistence: Employs in-memory storage (src/store.js) during backend Express execution and seamlessly falls back to browser localStorage when deployed statically on GitHub Pages.

3.2 Automated Test Suite Implementation (Task 3 - 10 Marks)

The test suite is written in tests/submission.test.js using Jest and Supertest to evaluate the HTTP contract of the submission API against the exact criteria in the lab mid specification:

Test Case Name Input Scenario Expected Behavior & Assertions
TC.01: Complete details and valid URL Valid student name, registration number, assignment title, and HTTPS repository link. HTTP 201 Created; record returned with ID; confirmed present in GET /api/submissions.
TC.02: Missing registration number Payload omitting regNo field. HTTP 400 Bad Request; error message contains "registration number"; store remains empty (count 0).
TC.03: Invalid submission URL Payload with ftp://not-a-valid-http-url. HTTP 400 Bad Request; error matches "submission url"; record is not saved.
TC.04: Missing name / title Payload missing student name or assignment title. HTTP 400 Bad Request; comprehensive field integrity rejection.

4. Task 4: Local HTTP Receiver & JSON Telemetry (14 Marks)

4.1 The Localhost Cloud Connectivity Problem & Solution

A critical architectural requirement in the lab mid is receiving the test report on localhost. However, GitHub Actions executes on remote Azure cloud runners; a cloud runner attempting to POST to http://localhost:5050 reaches only itself.

Reverse Tunnel Relay Solution
We implemented receiver/start-tunnel.js using Localtunnel (and compatible with Cloudflare Tunnel/ngrok). It exposes the local receiver on port 5050 via a secure public HTTPS endpoint (stored in GitHub Repository Secret RECEIVER_URL). The cloud runner sends telemetry across the internet directly into the local receiver!

4.2 Local Receiver Implementation (receiver/server.js)

  • Port & Route: Listens on port 5050; handles POST /report.
  • Disk Persistence: Atomically parses incoming JSON payloads and writes them directly to ./test-report.json.
  • Live Visual Dashboard: Serves an auto-refreshing status inspector on http://localhost:5050/ displaying repository name, branch, commit SHA, run ID, and test summary.
  • Guaranteed Delivery (if: always()): In .github/workflows/ci.yml, the reporting step runs under if: always() so that local records are updated on both passing and failing runs!
Figure 4.1: Local HTTP Receiver Dashboard showing real-time test report for a passing run.
Figure 4.2: Structured test-report.json schema saved automatically to local disk by the receiver.

5. Task 5: Complete Demonstration Workflow (4 Marks)

The lab mid requires a clear, 3-stage demonstration proving that the automated CI pipeline detects defects, reports failure details to the local computer, halts downstream deployments, and recovers upon bug resolution.

Stage 1: Initial Passing Run
Code pushed with all validation rules intact. The CI test suite passes (4/4 tests). The pipeline status turns green, the local receiver writes test-report.json with "overallStatus": "PASSED", and conditional GitHub Pages deployment executes.
Stage 2: Introduce Defect (Failing Run)
A regression was introduced in src/validator.js by commenting out the registration number check. Pushed to GitHub:
  • GitHub Actions test step fails on Test Case 2 (HTTP 201 received instead of 400).
  • Because of if: always(), the report is still delivered to localhost!
  • Local receiver dashboard updates to Status: FAILED (Total: 4, Passed: 3, Failed: 1).
  • GitHub Pages deployment step is completely skipped (protecting production!).
Stage 3: Fix Defect (Restored Run)
Validation restored in src/validator.js. Pushed to GitHub: pipeline turns green, local receiver updates test-report.json back to "overallStatus": "PASSED", and Pages deploys cleanly.
Figure 5.1: GitHub Actions defect run: test stage fails (red), Pages deploy skipped (gray), failure report transmitted.
Figure 5.2: Local HTTP receiver updating test-report.json on disk to Status: FAILED during the defect run.

6. Bonus Tasks: Conditional Deployment & Email Reporting (10 Marks)

6.1 Bonus Task 1: Conditional Deployment to GitHub Pages (5 Marks)

The application's frontend is deployed to GitHub Pages via an automated deployment job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Strict conditional execution is enforced: 

deploy:
  name: Conditional Deploy to GitHub Pages
  needs: test                                                        # Strict dependency on test job!
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push' # Only on main branch pushes
  environment:
    name: github-pages
    url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
    - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: './public'
    - uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

Verification Evidence: Live and operational at: https://coffeethebest.github.io/devops-lab-mid/. If any test fails, needs: test causes GitHub Actions to skip deployment, preserving the existing stable website.

Figure 6.1: Passing CI/CD pipeline showing both Test Execution and Conditional Pages Deployment.

6.2 Bonus Task 2: Automated Email Reporting (5 Marks)

An automated email reporter was built in scripts/send-email.js using Nodemailer. It transmits an HTML test digest and attaches the raw test-report.json artifact to the configured recipient (huzaifakhan.9139@gmail.com).

  • Execution Trigger: Runs under if: always() so emails are sent on both passing and failing runs.
  • Security: All credentials (EMAIL_USER, EMAIL_PASS, EMAIL_TO) are stored securely in GitHub Repository Secrets.
